# Michael Willox

[I measure what drives productivity and environmental performance, and test whether public policy works.]{.positioning}

[Senior Research Economist, Statistics Canada · PhD candidate in Economics, Brunel University London]{.roles}

I have more than twenty years of experience across five federal departments and agencies, including Finance Canada and Statistics Canada. I estimate productivity and efficiency from firm- and industry-level data, evaluate the effects of programs and policies, and build data products that businesses and governments use to make decisions.

## What I work on

-   **Productivity measurement.** Industry and business-sector productivity, Canada–U.S. comparisons, and benchmarking tools for firms.
-   **Environmental economics.** How carbon pricing and emissions affect firm efficiency, and environmentally adjusted productivity.
-   **Impact evaluation.** Causal estimates of program effects for federal departments and Crown corporations, including BDC and Export Development Canada.

## Featured work

::: grid
::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .feature-card}
### Why Canada's productivity growth fell behind the U.S. after 2001

[Gu & Willox (2023), *International Productivity Monitor* 45]{.venue}

Traces the divergence to the information and cultural industries and shows how limited competition held back productivity there and in the industries that depend on them.

[Read the paper →](http://csls.ca/ipm/45/IPM_45_Gu.pdf)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .feature-card}
### Do carbon taxes affect economic and environmental efficiency?

[Kumbhakar, Badunenko & Willox (2022), *Energy Economics* 115]{.venue}

Uses plant-level data on British Columbia manufacturers to show that a 1% higher carbon tax raised output efficiency by 0.5% and greenhouse gas efficiency by 0.2%.

[Read the paper →](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eneco.2022.106359)
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-4 .feature-card}
### Who used the Canada Emergency Wage Subsidy?

[Liu, Lu & Willox (2021), Statistics Canada, *Economic and Social Reports*]{.venue}

Examines which employer businesses took up Canada's largest pandemic support program in 2020, and how use varied by firm size and industry.

[Read the report →](https://doi.org/10.25318/36280001202100600006-eng)
:::
:::
